name: In-app purchase (StoreKit 2, Play Billing)
plain: Sells digital goods and subscriptions through the platform store.
meaning: The platform handles payment, receipts and refunds, and takes a commission. The store knows who buys what in every app.

android.prompt_ui: Google Play purchase sheet with auth
android.store_policy: Play: digital goods must use Play Billing unless a program allows alternatives; PBL 7 or 8 required for new releases
android.api_surface: Google Play Billing Library 7 and 8, ProductDetails, BillingClient
android.note: Fee 15 percent for first million dollars and subscriptions after year one; 30 percent standard. Epic settlement changes pending.

ios.prompt_ui: App Store purchase sheet with Face ID
ios.api_surface: StoreKit 2 Product, Transaction, AppTransaction (iOS 16); StoreKit Messages
ios.note: Small Business Program 15 percent; App Store Server API for refunds.

limits.headline: Can sell digital items and subscriptions, after you approve each purchase
limits.user_action: You tap Buy or Subscribe and confirm with Face ID, a fingerprint or a passcode
can: Charge you through the App Store or Google Play after you confirm
Offer subscriptions that renew until you cancel
Issue refunds through the store tools on iPhone
cannot: Charge you without a purchase sheet and your confirmation
Skip the store's fee, which is 15 or 30 percent in most cases
Cancel your subscription for you; that happens in your store account
limits.differs: iPhone uses StoreKit and Face ID. Android uses Play Billing and a Google Play purchase sheet. Store fees are 15 or 30 percent.

story.what_it_is: The store's built in way to sell subscriptions and digital goods inside an app.

marketing.name: In-App Purchase
marketing.pitch: Apple pitches In-App Purchase as a simple, secure way to sell digital goods and subscriptions in apps.

marketing.name: Google Play Billing
marketing.pitch: Google describes Play Billing as the system for selling digital products and subscriptions in apps.

story.for_you: You tap Subscribe and a store sheet asks for Face ID or a fingerprint. The charge goes on your account and you can manage or cancel it in settings.
story.for_makers: Makers get payments, receipts and refunds handled for them. The store keeps a commission, usually 15 to 30 percent, and knows who buys what in every app.

use_cases.example: A game sells gems and a battle pass with one tap.
A streaming app sells a monthly plan.
A notes app unlocks pro features once.
A dating app sells boosts and premium.
A language app sells a yearly plan.
A fraud team checks receipts to stop fake purchases.
A growth team measures which ad led to a first purchase.

story.android_note: Google takes 15 percent on the first million dollars and on subscriptions after year one. 30 percent is standard.
story.ios_note: Apple's Small Business Program lowers the fee to 15 percent. Purchases use Face ID.

technical_bounds: Apple 3.1.1 and Play rule: digital goods need store billing except where law or programs allow external options
Store holds card data, not the app

linkedin.how: Premium and Learning subscriptions are sold in app. Apple label lists Purchase History and Other Financial Info as Linked to You; Play lists purchase history and other financial info (optional).

history.change: Required for new apps on Play from Aug 2025
Play Billing Library 5 and later changes to subscriptions
